doc.title: Håkan Rydin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016

title: Pianist influences: McCoy Tyner, Herbie Hancock, Chick Corea, Keith Jarrett
summary: Rowe offers names; Rydin says Hancock, Tyner, Corea and Jarrett, plus Bill Evans, shaped his playing.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Let me run a couple of names by you and see if they mean anything. Ramsey Lewis?
Not so very much, yeah? Well of course I’ve heard it, that’s a great piano player.

Definitely. Definitely. Again, when I was at the age where you think about how you want to play, I had four musicians at the generation of McCoy. It was Herbie Hancock, it was McCoy Tyner, it was Chick Corea and it was Keith Jarrett. And then of course there was always Bill Evans. But I wanted to mix those four guys — I don’t mean strictly, but that was kind of deliberate. Those were my four most important.
